**Starts** once #136 is merged.

## Why

Joe can't see how the coordinator worked on a turn once it's over, except in the chat's raw view, which isn't saved. Agent evaluations (#53) also need traces to build on. The #132 spike traced the coordinator in Arize Phoenix, but only on Joe's machine, from `npm run chat`. This issue runs one Phoenix on the server, and sends it the traces of every web chat turn: from the live site, and from `npm run dev` on Joe's machine. So there's one place to see both. This issue is only about traces. Evaluations stay in #53.

A **trace** is the record of one turn. It's made of **spans**: one for the turn, and under it, in order, one for each model call and one for each tool call. A Phoenix **project** holds its own traces, sessions, and token totals.

## Design

- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), sections 2 (the server and its containers), 6 (local development), and 7 (deploys).
- [research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), sections 2.1 (Phoenix in Docker Compose), 2.2 (tracing a coordinator turn), and 3. The spike's code is on the [`spike/phoenix-evals`](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/tree/spike/phoenix-evals) branch.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 10.1 (the chat view and the raw view).

## Open questions

- ~~How does Joe's machine reach the server's Phoenix?~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-25: through an SSH tunnel, the same way it reaches the server's Postgres. Phoenix listens only on the server's `127.0.0.1:6006`, with no sign-in, so nothing new is open to the internet. Joe runs `ssh -N -L 6006:127.0.0.1:6006 root@projects.jjk3.com`. Then the local app sends traces to `http://127.0.0.1:6006`, and his browser opens the Phoenix UI at the same address. Putting Phoenix on the internet through Caddy was the other option. It would need Phoenix's sign-in, an API key for sending traces, and a second site, and every trace would be behind one login page.
- ~~How does the page show that traces aren't reaching Phoenix?~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-25: when the page loads, the app checks that it can reach Phoenix, and the page shows a green check or a red X. It's a reminder to bring up the tunnel when running locally, or to look into Phoenix on the server before starting a session. It doesn't check that each turn's spans arrived. The chat works the same either way. Spans that can't be sent are lost, with no retry.
- ~~How are the server's traces told apart from local ones?~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-25: two Phoenix projects. The server sends to `road-trip-agent`, and Joe's machine sends to `road-trip-agent-local`. Local traces are mostly test chats, from the local database, so they'd skew the server's session list and token totals if they were mixed. One project with a tag was the other option. It would need a filter typed in each time.
- How do the user's message and the right token counts get into each turn's trace? Phoenix's instrumentation for the Agent SDK shows the streamed prompt as `{}`, and leaves cache tokens out of its input count, so a 48,255-token turn shows as 8. The spike replaced it with spans from our own code, `TurnTrace`, which has the user's message, and each model call's thinking, tool calls, and tokens (research doc sections 2.2 and 3). The proposal is to bring `TurnTrace` over. Moved from #53 on 2026-10-25.

## Do

- **Run Phoenix on the server.** Add a `phoenix` service to `compose.yaml`, like the spike's (research doc section 2.1), with these changes:
  - It's in the `production` profile, like `backup`, so it starts only on the server. Locally, no Phoenix runs. The local app sends to the server's, through the tunnel.
  - Its port is published only on the server's `127.0.0.1:6006`. The server's app reaches it over the Compose network.
  - Its image is `arizephoenix/phoenix:20.26.0`, the spike's. Its data is a SQLite file in its own volume, `phoenix-data`, not in our Postgres, so it isn't in the nightly backup. Sign-in and Phoenix's own telemetry are off.
  - `ops/deploy.sh` doesn't change. Its image list is only for our private images, which need a sign-in to pull. Its `docker compose up` pulls Phoenix's public image on its own.
- **Trace each coordinator turn.** Bring `TurnTrace` (`src/agent/turn-trace.ts`) and its changes to `runTurnWithSdk` and `src/agent/turn-event.ts` over from the spike branch, with tests on fakes. Bring it as #136 leaves it, so a worker's spans go under the coordinator's `Agent` tool span once workers exist (#60, #61, #64). No worker exists yet, so tests use a fake worker's messages. Add the packages it needs at the spike's exact versions: `@arizeai/phoenix-otel` 2.3.0, `@opentelemetry/api` 1.9.1, and `@arizeai/openinference-semantic-conventions` 2.15.0. `@arizeai/phoenix-client` isn't needed for traces, so it stays with #53. Besides the spike's `session.id`, each turn's span gets the user's ID as `user.id`, so a trace shows whose chat it is.
- **Send the traces from the app and from `npm run chat`.** Both set up the tracer when they start, in `src/main.ts` and `src/chat.ts`, from two values in the environment: Phoenix's address and the project's name. Check them with Zod in `src/config/env.schema.ts`. `compose.yaml` sets them for the server's app container: `http://phoenix:6006` and `road-trip-agent`. So the server's `.env` doesn't change. Locally, `.env` has `http://127.0.0.1:6006` and `road-trip-agent-local`. Add both to `.env.example`. Spans are sent in batches, so flush them before the process ends.
- **Show whether Phoenix can be reached** when the page loads, with a green check or a red X, next to the line from `web/src/health-status.tsx`. Every user sees it. The app does the check, since it's what sends the traces, and on the server the browser can't reach Phoenix. When Phoenix can't be reached, nothing else changes: chat turns run as before, and the deploy's call to `/api/health` doesn't fail.
- **Write it down.** In the systems design: the new container, and how Phoenix is reached on the server and from Joe's machine, with the tunnel command. In the functional spec: the check or X on the page. In DEVELOPMENT.md section 2: bring up the tunnel before `npm run dev` or `npm run chat`, and open the Phoenix UI.
- **Merge and deploy,** then check the live site and local `npm run dev` yourself (Done when). Sign in as Claude Code's own Supabase user (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5), and send one chat turn to each through `/api`. Then check Phoenix through the tunnel, such as with its REST API. A Claude Code session can open the tunnel itself with the command above. That was checked on 2026-10-25. The green check and red X need no sign-in, since the health line shows before sign-in.

## Done when

- `npm run check` passes.
- After the deploy, with the tunnel up, a chat turn sent on `roadtrip.jjk3.com` shows up in Phoenix's `road-trip-agent` project. Its trace has the turn span, with the user's message and the reply, and the model call spans, with their thinking and tokens, and the tool spans, in order. The Sessions view groups the chat's turns.
- With the tunnel up, a chat turn sent to local `npm run dev` shows up in `road-trip-agent-local`.
- With the tunnel down, the local page shows the red X, and a chat turn still works. With it up, the page shows the green check.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment (DEVELOPMENT.md section 7), and Joe agrees by approving the PR.

## Why

Joe can't see how the coordinator worked on a turn once it's over, except in the chat's raw view, which isn't saved. Agent evaluations (#53) also need traces to build on. The #132 spike traced the coordinator in Arize Phoenix, but only on Joe's machine, from `npm run chat`. This issue runs one Phoenix on the server, and sends it the traces of every web chat turn: from the live site, and from `npm run dev` on Joe's machine. So there's one place to see both. This issue is only about traces. Evaluations stay in #53.

A **trace** is the record of one turn. It's made of **spans**: one for the turn, and under it, in order, one for each model call and one for each tool call. A Phoenix **project** holds its own traces, sessions, and token totals.

## Open questions

- ~~How does Joe's machine reach the server's Phoenix?~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-25: through an SSH tunnel, the same way it reaches the server's Postgres. Phoenix listens only on the server's `127.0.0.1:6006`, with no sign-in, so nothing new is open to the internet. Joe runs `ssh -N -L 6006:127.0.0.1:6006 root@projects.jjk3.com`. Then the local app sends traces to `http://127.0.0.1:6006`, and his browser opens the Phoenix UI at the same address. Putting Phoenix on the internet through Caddy was the other option. It would need Phoenix's sign-in, an API key for sending traces, and a second site, and every trace would be behind one login page.
- ~~How does the page show that traces aren't reaching Phoenix?~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-25: when the page loads, the app checks that it can reach Phoenix, and the page shows a green check or a red X. It's a reminder to bring up the tunnel when running locally, or to look into Phoenix on the server before starting a session. It doesn't check that each turn's spans arrived. The chat works the same either way. Spans that can't be sent are lost, with no retry.
- ~~How are the server's traces told apart from local ones?~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-25: two Phoenix projects. The server sends to `road-trip-agent`, and Joe's machine sends to `road-trip-agent-local`. Local traces are mostly test chats, from the local database, so they'd skew the server's session list and token totals if they were mixed. One project with a tag was the other option. It would need a filter typed in each time.
- How do the user's message and the right token counts get into each turn's trace? Phoenix's instrumentation for the Agent SDK shows the streamed prompt as `{}`, and leaves cache tokens out of its input count, so a 48,255-token turn shows as 8. The spike replaced it with spans from our own code, `TurnTrace`, which has the user's message, and each model call's thinking, tool calls, and tokens (research doc sections 2.2 and 3). The proposal is to bring `TurnTrace` over. Moved from #53 on 2026-10-25.
